extracted.intended_audience: New York state agency rulemaking officials and regulatory staff (those preparing notices, regulatory impact statements, and associated analyses)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluative standards from the New York State Administrative Procedure Act governing the content, timing, publication, distribution, and supporting analyses for proposed, revised, emergency and adopted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice period for public comment must be not less than sixty days after publication, or, if statute requires a public hearing prior to adoption, not less than five days after the date of the last public hearing scheduled to be held on the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding the above, when the notice contains only a description of subject/purpose/substance (see subparagraph (v) of paragraph (f)), the full text must be posted on a website and remain posted until adoption/revision/withdrawal/expiration (except certain narrow rule exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rule abbreviated process and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a notice is submitted solely for proposing a consensus rule, the agency may dispense with any requirement for public hearing and certain notice subparagraphs, provided the notice includes a statement setting forth a clear and concise explanation of the basis for the agency's determination that no person is likely to object to adoption as written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any public comment objects to adoption of a consensus rule, the agency must withdraw the notice and may resubmit complying with all relevant provisions. Major changes (as defined by public service law) may not be adopted as consensus rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional additional publications
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, the agency may also publish notice in newspapers of general circulation and in trade, industry or professional publications as selected by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in other outlets is discretionary and supplemental to state register publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice does not preclude earlier hearing initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of a notice in the state register does not preclude the initiation of a public hearing with respect to certain rules where notice otherwise consistent has been given; however, notice must be published within a reasonable time prior to the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies particularly to rules defined in subparagraph (ii) of paragraph (a) of subdivision two of section 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after withdrawn consensus rule must identify prior objections
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a notice of proposed rule making for a rule previously proposed as a consensus rule and withdrawn, the notice must identify the prior notice and briefly describe the objection(s) that caused the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transparency about prior objections to inform public and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall cite the statutory authority, including particular sections and subdivisions, under which the rule is proposed for adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation must be specific (sections and subdivisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – hearing logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must give the date, time and place of any public hearing or hearings which are scheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no hearings are scheduled, this should be reflected accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – physical accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must state whether or not the place of any public hearing or hearings shall be reasonably accessible to persons with a mobility impairment (defined in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of accessibility despite diligent effort does not affect actions or proceedings at such hearings; definition of 'persons with a mobility impairment' is provided in statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – interpreter services for deaf persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include a statement that interpreter services shall be made available to deaf persons, at no charge, upon written request to the designated agency representative within a reasonable time prior to any scheduled public hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested, the agency must appoint a qualified interpreter certified by a recognized national or New York state credentialing authority; agency may determine reasonable fee to charge the agency for interpreting services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – text vs. summary and website posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall contain the complete text of the proposed rule; provided, however, if such text exceeds two thousand words, the notice shall contain only a description of the subject, purpose and substance of such rule in less than two thousand words and shall identify the address of the website where the full text has been posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When full text is not included due to length, the notice must clearly identify the website and the posted full text must be maintained as required elsewhere in the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – regulatory impact statement inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include a regulatory impact statement prepared pursuant to section 202-A; if the statement exceeds two thousand words, the notice shall include only a summary of the statement in less than two thousand words and identify where the full text is posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 202-A for required contents of the regulatory impact statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – regulatory flexibility and rural area analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include a regulatory flexibility analysis and a rural area flexibility analysis prepared pursuant to sections 202-B and 202-BB; if any analysis exceeds two thousand words, the notice shall include only a summary under two thousand words and identify where the full text is posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 202-B and 202-BB for required contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – agency contact for documents and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall give the name, public office address and telephone number of an agency representative, knowledgeable on the proposed rule, from whom the complete text and any scientific or statistical study, report and analysis that served as the basis for the rule and supporting data, the regulatory impact statement, regulatory flexibility analysis, and rural area flexibility analysis may be obtained; from whom information about any public hearing may be obtained; and to whom written data, views and arguments may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must designate a single knowledgeable representative and provide complete contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of proposed rule making – additional statutory matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include any additional matter required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all provision: include anything else specifically required by other statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration of notice of proposed rule making
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain narrow classes of rule, a notice of proposed rule making shall expire and be ineffective for the purposes of this section unless the proposed rule is adopted and filed with the secretary of state within 365 days after the later of publication in the state register or the date of the last public hearing announced in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a notice expires the secretary of state shall publish a notice of expiration in the state register containing information determined in the secretary's discretion to serve public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of rule making by submission of revised notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If, within ninety days of the date on which a rule will expire, an agency submits a notice of revised rule making for the rule, the rule making will be continued for an additional ninety days beyond the date on which it would have expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of revised notice extends life of the pending rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of notice of proposed rule making – reasons required
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may withdraw a notice of proposed rule making and terminate a rule making proceeding by submitting a notice of withdrawal to the secretary of state for publication; such notice shall include a statement of the reason or reasons for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal must be published and must state the grounds for termination of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of revised rule making – timing and public comment opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to adoption of a rule, an agency shall submit a notice of revised rule making for any proposed rule which contains a substantial revision; the notice must appear in the state register at least thirty days prior to adoption and indicate the last date for submission of comments on the revised text, which shall be not less than thirty days after publication unless statute specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised notices are required for substantial changes and preserve the public's opportunity to comment on revised text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of public comment for revised rule making
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish and make available to the public an assessment of public comment for a rule revised pursuant to this subdivision, based upon written comments and comments presented at public hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment shall contain: (i) a summary and analysis of issues raised and significant alternatives suggested; (ii) a statement of reasons why any significant alternatives were not incorporated; (iii) description of any changes made in the rule as a result of such comments. If no comments received, notice shall state so. Subsequent assessments need only include comments not previously addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of revised rule making – contents list
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of revised rule making shall: cite statutory authority; contain complete revised text or description if >2000 words and identify website; identify substantial revisions; give date/time/place of hearings; include revised regulatory impact statement or summary if >2000 words and identify website; include revised regulatory flexibility and rural analyses or summaries and identify website; give agency representative contact info; state whether notice extends rule making period for additional 90 days; include assessment of public comment or summary if >2000 words; include any additional matter required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors proposed-notice requirements with added items specific to revisions and assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on revised notices for consensus rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may not submit a notice of revised rule making for a rule which has been proposed as a consensus rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus-rule procedural shortcuts preclude subsequent revised notices under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of adoption timing and prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency files a rule with the secretary of state it shall also submit a notice of adoption for publication in the state register; except as provided in subdivision six, an agency may not file a rule or submit a notice of adoption unless the agency has previously submitted a notice of proposed rule making and complied with the provisions of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing/adoption is generally conditioned on prior compliance with notice-and-comment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of public comment for adopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain narrow rules, each agency shall publish and make available an assessment of public comment for a rule adopted, containing: (i) summary and analysis of issues and significant alternatives; (ii) statement of reasons why significant alternatives were not incorporated; (iii) description of any changes made in rule as a result of comments. If cost estimates differed significantly, the assessment shall summarize the agency's assessment of such estimates. Legislative committee/legislator comments are considered public comment and must be summarized and analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment content mirrors revised-notice assessment; includes handling of differing cost estimates and legislative comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of notice of adoption – contents list
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of adoption shall: cite statutory authority; contain the complete text of the rule as adopted or a description if >2000 words; state whether there have been any changes compared with the latest published proposed text and cite sections changed; give the effective date; include revised regulatory impact statement (or summary); include revised regulatory flexibility and rural analyses (or summaries); include assessment of public comment (or summary); give agency representative contact info for obtaining texts and analyses; state whether any notice of revised rule making had been submitted and dates; include any additional matter required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all materials and changes are documented and accessible; summaries permitted if >2000 words and full texts posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoption – authority and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds immediate adoption necessary for preservation of public health, safety or general welfare and that compliance with normal requirements would be contrary to the public interest, the agency may adopt the rule on an emergency basis; such emergency rule shall not remain in effect longer than ninety days after filing unless within that time the agency complies with subdivision one and adopts the rule, with special readoption limits (subsequent readoptions no longer than sixty days etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain categories (security authorizations/corporate/financial structures) may be excepted from expiration if statute does not require hearing and agency finds subsequent notice would frustrate purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of emergency adoption – required findings and description
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of emergency adoption shall: cite statutory authority; state whether it also constitutes notice of proposed rule making (and if so give hearing info); state whether it constitutes notice of revised rule making (and if so include required info); contain findings required by emergency paragraphs and include a statement fully describing specific reasons and facts/circumstances on which findings are based — at minimum: description of nature and location of the need; description of cause, consequences, and expected duration; explanation why compliance with regular requirements would be contrary to public interest; explanation why public should be given less than minimum period for notice and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be comprehensive and include factual support for emergency adoption rather than conclusory assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of emergency adoption – other required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of emergency adoption shall give the effective date; state the specific date the emergency rule will expire; contain the complete adopted text or a description with website if >2000 words; include a regulatory impact statement or statement that it will appear in State Register within 30 days (or summaries if >2000 words); include regulatory flexibility and rural analyses or statement they will appear within 30 days (or summaries); give agency representative contact info; include any additional matter required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only a description is provided in the notice, the full text must be posted on a website as soon as practicable and not later than the date the notice is published in the state register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of rulemaking materials to officials and public
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall transmit a copy of any rulemaking notice to the governor, the temporary president of the senate, the speaker of the assembly and the administrative regulations review commission at the time such notice is submitted to the secretary of state, including complete rule text, regulatory impact statement, regulatory flexibility analysis, rural area flexibility analysis or revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also make copies available to the public at time submitted and send on request; agencies must notify persons who requested notice; written requests expire annually (Dec 31) with renewal option; electronic requests do not expire; agencies may charge fee for mailed notices but not for electronic notices; alternatively the agency may provide a link to the website section containing the full text instead of sending document electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule text formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete text of any proposed or adopted rule shall identify new language by underscoring or italics, enclose in brackets any words which are to be deleted, and give the citation of any rule which is to be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting clarifies additions and deletions; exceptions exist for certain short rule classes and for publications other than the state register (see paragraph (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on including full text in certain notices/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may, with regard to certain classes of rules or notices published outside the state register, elect to include either the complete text (if 2000 words or less) or a description of the subject, purpose and substance (if exceeding 2000 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific exceptions apply to certain rule types defined elsewhere in the statute; agencies should follow those class definitions when electing to use summaries rather than full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-count determination exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining if the length of the text of a rule exceeds two thousand words for publication purposes, the word count shall exclude any previously published portion of the rule which is precisely identified in the text pursuant to the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps avoid double-counting previously published language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website posting and notice accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a notice refers to any rule, text or other information posted on a state-entity-maintained website in lieu of publication, the text/information shall be posted not later than the date the notice is published in the state register and, to the extent practicable, maintained on such website during the entire period the notice is effective; the notice must provide sufficient information to enable the public to access such information without extensive searching and conform to guidance prescribed by the secretary of state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of state will develop guidance for online posting; notices must give specific website addresses and sufficient access information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review time limit for procedural noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A proceeding may be commenced to contest a rule on the grounds of noncompliance with the procedural requirements of this section and specified sections, provided such proceeding is commenced within four months from the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rule must be promulgated in substantial compliance with the provisions; inadvertent failure to send notice to any person shall not invalidate a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of State duties regarding notices and online access
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall prescribe standard forms for notices; promptly review each notice submitted; reject notices not in substantial compliance and advise corrective action; publish all required notices and statements in the state register; and prescribe guidance for online posting of text and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of state may also publish an electronic copy of the state register and must provide direct links from the electronic register to agency-provided email addresses to permit immediate submission of comments; however, neither the secretary nor the agency is responsible for delivery failures caused by hardware/software incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – agency duty to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall, except as provided in subdivision five, issue a regulatory impact statement for a rule proposed for adoption or a rule adopted on an emergency basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 202-A specifies the required components of the regulatory impact statement and allows certain consolidated filings to reduce paperwork; exemptions include technical amendments and certain consensus or narrowly defined rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – statutory authority analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory impact statement shall contain a statement analyzing the statutory authority for the rule, including the agency's interpretation of the legislative objectives of such authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how statutory authority supports the rule and interpretive choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – needs and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall set forth the purpose of, necessity for, and benefits derived from the rule; provide a citation and summary (not to exceed 500 words) of each scientific or statistical study, report or analysis that served as the basis for the rule, explain how it was used to determine necessity/benefits, and name the person that produced each study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries of supporting studies are limited to 500 words each and must identify authors to permit verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall detail projected costs indicating: (i) costs for implementation of and continuing compliance by regulated persons; (ii) costs for implementation and continued administration to the agency and to the state and local governments; and (iii) the information and methodology upon which the cost analysis is based; or where full costs cannot be provided, the agency's best estimate with explanation and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency cannot fully provide cost figures, it must provide best estimates and explain why complete information cannot be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – paperwork
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall describe the need for any reporting requirements, including forms and other paperwork, resulting from the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe burden and necessity of reporting to justify paperwork imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – local government mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall describe any program, service, duty or responsibility imposed by the rule upon counties, cities, towns, villages, school districts, fire districts or other special districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify obligations placed on local governments and describe impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – duplication and conflict identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall identify relevant state and federal rules and legal requirements that may duplicate, overlap or conflict with the rule; if duplication/overlap/conflict exists, the statement should identify efforts the agency has or will undertake to resolve or minimize such impacts (waivers, amendments, MOUs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe steps to mitigate duplication/overlap/conflict for regulated persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – alternatives considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall indicate whether any significant alternatives to the rule were considered, discuss such alternatives and explain why they were not incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document consideration of alternatives and rationale for rejecting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – federal standards comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall identify whether the rule exceeds any minimum federal standards for the same or similar subject areas and, if so, explain why it exceeds such standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for more stringent state standards relative to federal minimums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement – compliance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement shall indicate the estimated period of time necessary to enable regulated persons to achieve compliance with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic timelines and consider phased compliance if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of related regulatory impact statements
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may consider a series of closely related and simultaneously proposed rules as one rule for the purpose of submitting a consolidated regulatory impact statement and may submit a consolidated statement for any series of virtually identical rules proposed in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation reduces paperwork burden when rules are related or largely identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from regulatory impact statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may claim an exemption for a rule that involves only a technical amendment provided the agency states the reason in the notice; certain narrowly defined rules and consensus rules are exempt as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption claims must be justified in the notice of proposed rule making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised regulatory impact statement required when information changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall issue a revised regulatory impact statement when: (a) information in the statement is inadequate/incomplete; (b) a proposed rule contains substantial revisions necessitating modification of the statement; or (c) there are no substantial revisions but adopted text changes necessitate modification. Revised statements shall be submitted as soon as practicable and may be summarized if >2000 words with full text posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised statements must describe reasons for changes and include necessary modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility analysis – duty to minimize impacts on small businesses/local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, an agency shall consider approaches that accomplish statutory objectives while minimizing adverse economic impact on small businesses and local governments; approaches include differing compliance/reporting requirements or timetables, use of performance rather than design standards, or exemptions for small businesses/local governments where public safety is not endangered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should show agency considered less burdensome alternatives and tailored requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility analysis – cure period for penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules requiring a regulatory flexibility analysis that establish or modify violations or penalties, the agency shall include a cure period or other opportunity for ameliorative action that prevents imposition of penalties upon successful completion, or explain why no cure period was included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cure periods mitigate harsh impacts on small entities; absence must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility analysis – issuance and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing or adopting a rule on an emergency basis, the agency shall issue a regulatory flexibility analysis and submit a copy (and any finding and reasons) to the governor, legislative leaders, office of business permits and regulatory assistance, and the administrative regulations review commission at time of submission to the secretary of state; upon written request, a copy shall be sent to any other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely distribution to listed officials and make accessible on request.
